messages:
alex: Heads-up — nightly perf (master build) shows steady RSS growth on long-seq bench, ~25% higher after 10k requests. Possible allocator fragmentation / churn. cc @maria @jon :eyes:

maria: which build tag? CI or local repro?

alex: CI artifact `redwood-runtime:2026-03-10-master` — I ran `bench/long_seq` on a c6i-large-ish VM. Repro command I used:
```
./bin/bench --workload long_seq --requests 10000 --concurrency 8 --profile heap
```
There are a couple OOMs at ~8k requests on the smallest test size.

jon: can you upload the heap profile and the jemalloc stats? Fragmentation sounds likely. Also did the KVCache change land recently?

alex: uploaded profile to s3: https://s3.redwood.internal/alloc/heap-20260310.pb.gz. jemalloc stats attached in same folder. The most frequent allocation size looks like ~512 bytes from KVCache::insert (stack shows `kv_cache.cpp:198`).

sara: I can run an A/B with system malloc vs jemalloc and one with the patch that landed in PR #2345 (KVCache eviction tweak). Want me to do both? :+1:

maria: yes run both. also try toggling extent hooks / mmap behavior. For jemalloc use `MALLOC_CONF"narenas:4,lg_dirty_mult:16,decay_time:1"` and collect `jeprof`/`jeinfo`.

alex: good call. quick note: the regression wasn't obvious on short runs (100 reqs) — only on sustained loads. So sampling in perf CI might miss it. Can we add a long-run smoke in nightly?

alloc-bot: CI job triggered: `perf-longseq-master-1779600100` queued. Will post results when finished.

jon: aside — I noticed recent use of `std::pmr::monotonic_buffer_resource` in the request parser PR. If that buffer is per-request and not reused, it can blow up quickly. Alex, does KVCache allocate from that or from heap?

alex: KVCache uses small-object allocations via `std::allocator` right now. The parser change shouldn't touch it but could increase peak resident if allocations overlap. I'll add an instrumented run that logs peak RSS per stage.

maria: schedule: sara will run A/B (jemalloc vs system) + PR rollback at 11:00 PT, jon will add high-frequency jemalloc stats collector, alex will rerun with parser instrumentation and upload outputs. If we still see OOMs, fallback option: reduce shard size and enable early eviction.

sara: running now. baseline perf command I'm using:
```
MALLOC_CONF"narenas:8,decay_time:1" ./bin/bench --workload long_seq --requests 10000 --concurrency 8 --collect-heap
```
I'll post logs & `smaps` after finishing.

jon: also add `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libtcmalloc_minimal.so.4` run so we can compare tcmalloc behavior.

alex: pinging reviewers on #2345 — might need a revert if this maps to KVCache churn.

maria: if the fragmentation is confirmed, we should add a small 1% rollout of an allocator config tweak in Dedicated to validate without full rollout.

alloc-bot: perf-longseq-master-1779600100 completed at 1779600300. Results: +22% median RSS, +28% 95p, 2 OOMs recorded. Artifacts uploaded to https://s3.redwood.internal/alloc/perf/1779600100/

alex: thanks. I'll grab the artifacts and start a heapstack diff. If anyone finds a quick mitigation (decay_time / arena tuning) please post here.

maria: noted — I'll try `decay_time:10` and `lg_dirty_mult:0` next to encourage purging; if that reduces RSS we'll prepare a config rollout.

alex: appreciate it. tagging @oncall-runtime in case customer-facing workloads are impacted.

sara: posted initial comparison (jemalloc vs system vs tcmalloc) in the S3 folder. Jemalloc looks worst for fragmentation; tcmalloc kept lower RSS but higher CPU. Sharing graphs shortly. :bar_chart:

jon: great. next steps: 1) reproduce locally with exact artifacts, 2) run jemalloc tuning, 3) consider KVCache allocator pool to avoid many small mallocs. I can prototype a slab allocator for 512B objects if the data supports it.

alex: sounds good. I'll update the PR and attach the heap diffs. Thanks all.
